messages:
alex: Customer (Wavefront Inc) reports streaming responses from /v1/stream are frequently missing the final JSON object — output ends mid-object or with no finish_reason. They say it started last week after moving to a smaller billing tier. Repro attached below.

alex: Repro steps (curl):
```
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \\  
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\  
  https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/stream?model=base-open-8k \  
  -d '{"prompt":"say hi repeatedly","max_tokens":512,"stream":true}'
```

alex: What we see: stream starts fine, several data: events with partial JSON, then a short silence and connection closed from client side. Last event sometimes is a partial JSON like `{"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"..."}` with no closing braces and no finish_reason.

maria: Customer logs (proxy side):
```
[2026-03-15T14:12:03Z] proxy: upstream CONNECT id=3
[2026-03-15T14:12:10Z] proxy: upstream RST_STREAM id=3 code=INTERNAL_ERROR
[2026-03-15T14:12:10Z] tcp: client closed connection
```
maria: They also show a 1s auth rotation hitting the same second: token rotate triggered while stream active.

jamie: Quick triage notes: partial outputs + RST_STREAM often mean upstream (our runtime) closed the stream mid-response or proxy applied an idle/buffer timeout. finish_reason missing can be caused if the final event (we emit `data: {"finish_reason":"stop"}`) never reaches client.

jamie: Questions for customer:
- Did the issue begin right after billing tier change or coincident with any config changes on your side (proxy timeouts, connection pool sizes)?
- Can you share raw tcpdump showing the FIN/RST?

alex: Customer says they did not change their proxy; billing change was on our end (reduced concurrency). They suspect requests are being routed to a different pool that may be preempting long-lived streams.

eng-runtime-bot: Automated check: current serving pool for tenant wavefront-001 has preemptive eviction enabled on low tier. Last 24h shows 18 stream evictions correlated with scale-down windows.

sre_kim: That matches. If serving nodes are preempted while KV cache is active, connections could be reset. Two mitigation ideas:
1) Add a server-side keepalive and ensure we flush final event before terminating connection.
2) Use graceful drain on instance recycle to allow streams to finish or be proxied to fallback model.

maria: Repro attempt from our side with shorter stream length (max_tokens 50) worked fine. Repro with long stream (max_tokens 2048) hit the issue after ~120s consistently. curl output shows final chunk absent.

jamie: Potentially related: auth token rotation at minute boundaries — if the auth middleware rejects a streaming request in-progress after rotation, client will see abrupt close. Need to check our token-refresh handling in the streaming path.

alex: Customer also reported that when they retry with reconnect/resume header the resumed stream contains a leftover trailing comma `...,]` causing JSON parse errors in their client. So two bugs: truncated final event and malformed resume payload.

sre_kim: Action items:
- Eng-runtime: add logs marking emission of final event (finish_reason) and flush/close sequence. Include correlation id header X-Redwood-Trace.
- Infra: audit preemptive eviction windows for dedicated pools and disable aggressive kills for tenants with active streams.
- Support: ask customer to provide tcpdump + the exact time of the events so we can match with trace ids.
- Eng-runtime: check auth-rotation handshake path for streaming connections; ensure rotation does not force RST without graceful close.

eng-runtime-bot: Created internal issue RUNTIME-4523 linking traces 2807659999-1..2807659999-7 and noting correlation with eviction events.

maria: Temporary workaround for customer: reduce stream duration (lower max_tokens), set client-side reconnect with dedup/resume that tolerates trailing commas, and add keepalive pings every 20s. Provided them example snippet.

alex: Customer follows up — they can reproduce reliably if they start a 2-3 minute stream and then trigger a 30s scale event (we simulated by draining one instance). I suggested we run a canary fix that delays eviction until active streams drain or we proxy them.

jamie: Also add a post-emit flush to the SSE writer: ensure we call writer.Flush() and wait for ACK or small timeout before closing. Without that the final bytes can be stuck in TLS buffer in the worker and lost when process exits.

alex: I'll keep the customer updated and attach the issue link. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0315-wavefront-stream-truncation, severity=medium, owner=eng-runtime.
